Summarize the pros and cons in a table:

Heat pumps move heat instead of generating it, so they can deliver two to four units of heat for every unit of electricity they use. That makes them cheaper to run than electric resistance heating and often cheaper than gas, depending on local prices. They also provide cooling in summer. On the downside, upfront costs are high, typically several times the cost of a new furnace, though rebates can offset part of it. Older models lose efficiency in very cold weather, and installation in older homes may require electrical upgrades or better insulation.

Can you summarize this?

The lighthouse keeper had not spoken to anyone in eleven days when the boat appeared. It was small, painted a faded yellow, and it drifted rather than sailed. She watched it through the brass telescope for an hour before deciding it was empty. When it finally bumped against the rocks below, she climbed down and found a single envelope tucked under the bench, addressed to her in her late husband's handwriting. She did not open it that night. She made tea, lit the lamp, and set the envelope on the table, where it stayed until morning.

Summarize this research abstract in plain language:

We conducted a randomized trial of 200 adults with mild insomnia to test whether a 20-minute evening walk improves sleep quality. Participants (120 women and 95 men) were assigned to either a walking group or a control group for eight weeks. The walking group reported falling asleep 11 minutes faster on average and rated their sleep quality higher on a standard questionnaire. No differences were found in total sleep time. We conclude that brief evening walks may modestly improve sleep onset in adults with mild insomnia.

Summarize this:

The human skeleton is a remarkable structure. Babies are born with exactly 206 bones, the same number as adults, which is why their skeletons are so flexible. Bones are living tissue: they constantly break down and rebuild, and the entire skeleton is replaced roughly every ten years. The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the body, while the stapes in the middle ear is the smallest.

What's the main argument here?

Cities spend heavily on building new roads to reduce traffic, but decades of evidence show that new lanes fill up within a few years, a pattern called induced demand. When driving gets easier, people drive more: they take trips they would have skipped, move farther from work, or switch from transit. The same money spent on frequent buses, protected bike lanes, and denser housing near jobs would do more to cut commute times. Building our way out of congestion has been tried for seventy years, and it has not worked.
